pages.title: Suicide prevention: how to get help now
pages.text: If you are having thoughts of suicide, help is available. Trained counsellors are on the line day and night. Self-harm is not something you have to face alone.

pages.title: Finding a domestic violence shelter near you
pages.text: Leaving an abusive partner is dangerous. Domestic violence advocates can help you build a safety plan and find emergency housing tonight.

pages.title: Recognising the early signs of an eating disorder
pages.text: Anorexia and bulimia often begin quietly. A person may restrict food, exercise compulsively, or withdraw from meals with others.

pages.title: After a sexual assault: your options
pages.text: Survivors of rape and sexual assault can seek medical care, report to police, or do neither. Advocates are available to explain each option without pressure.

pages.title: Breaking: mass shooting reported downtown
pages.text: Police responded to reports of a mass shooting this afternoon. Officials have not confirmed casualties. The area remains closed.

pages.title: Living with grief after a sudden death
pages.text: Grief after a sudden bereavement does not follow stages. Many people describe trauma symptoms months later, long after others expect them to have moved on.

pages.title: I don't want to be here anymore
pages.text: Some nights I think about ending it all. I don't have a plan exactly, I just want the noise to stop and for everything to be over.

pages.title: Detoxing from alcohol at home is dangerous
pages.text: Withdrawal from heavy drinking can cause seizures. People in recovery from addiction should not attempt an unsupervised detox.

pages.title: What to expect after a miscarriage
pages.text: Pregnancy loss in the first trimester is common and rarely anyone's fault. Physical recovery takes days; the rest takes longer.

pages.title: Talking to your family about a terminal diagnosis
pages.text: A palliative care team can help you decide what to say and when. Hospice does not mean giving up on comfort.

pages.title: Prevención del suicidio: líneas de ayuda
pages.text: Si tienes pensamientos de quitarte la vida, hay ayuda disponible. Los consejeros atienden a cualquier hora del día.

pages.title: Recognising the signs of an opioid overdose
pages.text: Someone who has taken too much of a drug may become unresponsive or stop breathing normally. Naloxone can reverse the effects within minutes if administered in time. Call emergency services immediately.

pages.title: What to do if a coworker won't stop harassing you
pages.text: Unwanted comments, following you between meetings, or messages that don't stop after you've asked can constitute harassment. Documenting every incident with dates and witnesses makes a formal complaint to HR far stronger.

pages.title: Finding a shelter bed on short notice
pages.text: Losing stable housing can happen faster than people expect after a job loss or a medical bill. Most cities keep an intake line open around the clock, and many shelters do not require identification to get a bed for the night.

pages.title: The first ninety days after release from prison
pages.text: Finding an apartment that will rent to someone with a record, opening a bank account without a permanent address, and reconnecting with family are the hardest parts of the first three months. Reentry programs can help with all three.

pages.title: Some days I don't know how to make the pain stop
pages.text: I've started doing things to my own body when it gets too loud in my head. It's not about wanting attention, it's the only thing that makes the noise quiet for a minute. I know it's not sustainable but I don't know what else to do.

pages.title: He says sorry every time, and every time I believe him a little less
pages.text: The apologies used to work. Now I flinch before he even raises his voice, and I've started keeping a bag packed in the closet just in case. I haven't told anyone because I don't know how to say it out loud.

pages.title: Writing letters to people I haven't said goodbye to yet
pages.text: I keep starting them and not finishing them. Part of me wants everything to just stop, permanently, and I've been thinking about how that would actually happen more than I'd like to admit.

pages.title: Violence conjugale : comment obtenir de l'aide
pages.text: Si vous vivez dans une relation où votre partenaire vous fait du mal, des conseillers sont disponibles vingt-quatre heures sur vingt-quatre pour vous aider à trouver un endroit sûr.

pages.title: Wenn du daran denkst, dir selbst wehzutun
pages.text: Manche Menschen haben Gedanken, sich selbst zu verletzen, wenn alles zu viel wird. Du bist nicht allein damit, und es gibt Beratungsstellen, die rund um die Uhr erreichbar sind.

pages.title: Como reconhecer os sinais de abuso em um relacionamento
pages.text: Um parceiro que controla suas finanças, isola você de amigos e familiares, ou ameaça machucar você são sinais de alerta. Buscar ajuda não significa que você fracassou.

pages.title: What it's like living with untreated trauma
pages.text: Something happened years ago that I've never been able to talk about. It still shapes how I react to loud noises, to being touched without warning, to feeling trapped in a room. I don't have a name for what I need, just a sense that I can't keep carrying it alone.

pages.title: The mornings I can't make myself get out of bed
pages.text: It's been weeks since anything felt like it was worth doing. What started as a rough patch has settled into something that feels more like depression, but I haven't told anyone how bad the mornings actually are. I don't know how to explain this to anyone.

pages.title: I think what happened to me as a kid still counts, even though it was a long time ago
pages.text: I never told anyone what my stepfather did when I was young. I've read that it counts as abuse even without bruises, but part of me still feels like I'm overreacting by calling it that.

pages.title: Nobody checks on you after the funeral is over
pages.text: Everyone showed up for the first week. Now it's been two months and I'm still not sleeping, still setting two coffee cups out of habit, and nobody calls anymore because they think the bereavement is supposed to be finished by now. It isn't.

pages.title: Community vigil planned after downtown terrorism attack
pages.text: City officials confirmed the explosion near the transit hub was an act of terrorism. A vigil is planned for tomorrow evening. Counselling services have been made available for anyone affected.

pages.title: Self-harm recovery: what actually helped me stop
pages.text: I spent three years relying on self-harm to cope before I found a therapist who didn't flinch when I told her. Recovery wasn't linear, and I still have urges sometimes, but I have better tools now than I did then.

pages.title: My relapse after four years of eating disorder recovery
pages.text: I thought I was done thinking about food this way. The eating disorder came back quietly, through small rules I told myself didn't count. I'm back in treatment now and telling people this time instead of hiding it.

pages.title: The grief never really left, it just stopped being loud
pages.text: The trauma of losing my brother didn't end when the funeral did. Some anniversaries hit harder than others, and grief still shows up in ways I don't expect, months and years later.

pages.title: The Great Depression: causes and consequences
pages.text: The Great Depression began with the 1929 crash. Unemployment reached twenty-five percent and the resulting economic depression reshaped a generation of policy.

pages.title: Grief counselling degree programs, ranked
pages.text: A master's in grief counselling prepares graduates for hospice and bereavement work. Programs vary in clinical hours, tuition, and licensure pathway.

pages.title: How the Armenian genocide is taught in schools
pages.text: Historians debate how the genocide should appear in secondary curricula. The question is one of pedagogy and national memory more than of fact.

pages.title: Chapter 12: Eating disorders — a clinical overview
pages.text: This chapter surveys the diagnostic criteria for anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa, prevalence by cohort, and the evidence base for family-based treatment.

pages.title: Blunt force trauma testing in helmet design
pages.text: Impact trauma is measured with an instrumented headform. Engineers compare abuse-case loads against the standard's threshold.

pages.title: Is the housing market in a depression or a correction?
pages.text: Analysts disagree on whether the current slump counts as a depression. Volume is down, prices are flat, and inventory is rising.

pages.title: The best weeknight tomato pasta
pages.text: Blister the tomatoes in olive oil until they collapse. Add garlic, a splash of pasta water, and finish off the heat with basil.

pages.title: Understanding lifetimes in Rust
pages.text: A lifetime annotation tells the borrow checker how long a reference is valid. Most of the time elision handles it for you.

pages.title: Transfer window: the ten deals still on the table
pages.text: Clubs have until Monday to complete business. Two of the moves below hinge on a medical, and one on a manager who has not yet been appointed.

pages.title: New research on trauma-informed classroom design
pages.text: Architects are increasingly incorporating trauma-informed design principles into school buildings, including softer lighting and clearer sightlines. The approach draws on research about how physical space affects stress responses.

pages.title: A new university course on genocide prevention policy
pages.text: The political science department is launching a course examining the international frameworks meant to prevent genocide, drawing on case studies from the twentieth century onward.

pages.title: Antitrust regulators crack down on abuse of market dominance
pages.text: Regulators fined the company for what they called a clear abuse of its dominant position in the cloud computing market. The company says it will appeal.

pages.title: Could a 1930s-style depression happen again?
pages.text: Economists are split on whether current conditions resemble the depression of the interwar years closely enough to draw useful lessons, or whether the comparison is more rhetorical than analytical.

pages.title: Crisis management training for new managers
pages.text: The workshop covers how to keep a team functioning when a mental health crisis affects a colleague, including what a manager should and should not attempt to handle personally.

pages.title: How company bereavement leave policies compare
pages.text: Most employers offer between three and five days of bereavement leave, though policies vary widely on which relationships qualify and whether leave is paid.

pages.title: Getting a reliable rise from your sourdough starter
pages.text: Feed your starter at the same time each day and keep it somewhere consistently warm. A sluggish rise is almost always a temperature or hydration problem, not a dead starter.

pages.title: CSS grid vs flexbox: when to use which
pages.text: Grid is for two-dimensional layouts where you care about both rows and columns at once. Flexbox is for one-dimensional flows. Most real layouts end up using both.

pages.title: Building a sixteen-week marathon training plan
pages.text: Most plans peak around week twelve before tapering. The long run should increase gradually, and cutting it short when you're tired is usually smarter than pushing through.
